answer: A scripted farm therefore has to pad 191 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is written down against the haven challenge, the horizon audit can replay the quill history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 5 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
